label: PF Backlog 217
title: Backend: sensor/IoT capability pack + ingest adapters (MQTT/serial/BLE/Modbus/CAN) + time-series/anomaly models
body:
## Problem / why
IoT/sensor products are a listed modality but have no pack, no ingest, no store, and no time-series
models -- so they cannot be built. Sensors are data STREAMS, not media files.

## Goal & value
A `sensor` capability pack that, only when the idea needs it, enables device ingest, a time-series
store, forecasting/anomaly models, and a sensor-analyst agent -- all with permissive tooling.

## In scope
- **Ingest adapters:** MQTT (`paho-mqtt`), serial (`pyserial`), BLE (`bleak`), Modbus
  (`pymodbus`/`minimalmodbus`), CAN (`python-can`, LGPL), HTTP/REST, CSV/Parquet backfill.
- **Store:** Parquet/InfluxDB (client MIT) time-series store; register in store-registry.json.
  Grafana stays EXTERNAL (AGPL, never embedded).
- **Models (open-weights, permissive):** anomaly (IsolationForest, autoencoder/TSB-AE),
  forecasting (DLinear, N-BEATS, PatchTST, TimesNet, Chronos, Moirai); TinyML export (TFLite Micro).
- **Kinds:** `timeseries` (forecast), `sensor` (anomaly/classify); **fusion** (sensor+vision) as stretch.
- **Agent:** `sensor-analyst` (+ knowledge/skills), gated by the pack; capability pack entries in
  config/capability-packs.json.
- **QA:** range/rate checks, gap detection, drift alerts.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- An IoT idea enables the sensor pack (ingest+models+agent active); a plain app enables none.
- End-to-end: replay a CSV stream -> anomaly flagged + forecast produced as artifacts.
- All bundled tools/models are permissive (no GPL/AGPL embedded).

## Verification / test plan
- Unit: ingest adapter contract with a fake broker; model wrapper on a fixture series.
- Integration: CSV replay -> anomaly + forecast artifact; wired_audit green.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Reuse-first: extend core/capability_packs.py and config/capability-packs.json with a new 'sensor' capability pack entry. Reuse core/capability_bridge.py for pack-to-agent wiring. Extend core/intake_adapters.py with ingest adapter contract implementations (MQTT, serial, BLE, Modbus, CAN, HTTP, CSV/Parquet). Register time-series store in config/store-registry.json (or equivalent existing registry). Add anomaly + forecasting model wrappers following the existing generator_adapter pattern in core/generator_adapters.py. Add 'sensor-analyst' agent gated by the sensor pack. Only create NEW modules inside the sensor pack namespace (e.g., core/sensor_ingest.py, core/sensor_models.py) — do not create a new top-level framework.

RELATED: BI-0209 (sibling pack — pattern template for pack structure)

BLOCKS: nothing current; this pack may later BLOCK a sensor fusion item (stretch scope).
conflict_findings: config/capability-packs.json is shared with BI-0209 (OCR pack) — coordinate entries to avoid merge conflicts.
core/intake_adapters.py and core/generator_adapters.py may be concurrently edited by the OCR pack work — serialize or coordinate PRs.
config/agent-capability-vector.json shared with other agent-pack additions.
duplication_findings: BI-0185 (EPIC: Multi-modal orchestration / capability packs) is the parent epic — this item is a child pack within it, not a duplicate.
BI-0209 (OCR/document pack) is a sibling pack; it provides the template pattern for a new capability pack — reuse its pack structure, do not duplicate it.
BI-0180 (model-tier drift reconciliation) may need to be updated to include the new sensor model IDs in the model registry — coordinate, don't duplicate.
No existing sensor/IoT ingest adapter or time-series store found in candidate code.
analysis.rationale: High confidence because the item is very well specified with clear acceptance criteria and a strong candidate-code reuse list. The capability-pack framework (capability_packs.py, capability_bridge.py, config/capability-packs.json) already exists — the sensor pack plugs into it. New code is needed for ingest adapters and model wrappers, but within the established framework, not a new framework.
assumptions: config/capability-packs.json is the single registry for pack definitions (confirmed by item body).
core/capability_bridge.py and core/capability_packs.py provide the framework into which a new pack plugs in without modification (or with minimal extension).
All named models (IsolationForest, DLinear, N-BEATS, PatchTST, TimesNet, Chronos, Moirai) are permissive (MIT/Apache) — confirm Chronos and Moirai licenses.
Grafana stays external per item constraint — no embedding needed.
CSV/Parquet replay is sufficient for deterministic CI testing without live hardware.
risks: Many third-party IoT libraries (paho-mqtt, pyserial, bleak, pymodbus, python-can) expand dependency surface and compatibility risk.
python-can is LGPL — license compliance must be confirmed for bundling; item already flags it as a concern.
Time-series models (PatchTST, Chronos, Moirai) are large — packaging and cold-start performance may be an issue.
MQTT/serial/BLE hardware cannot be tested in CI without fakes — fake-broker testing is required but non-trivial.
Scope is large (6 ingest adapters + store + multiple models + agent) — risk of an over-long PR.
evidence: Candidate code: capability_bridge.py, capability_packs.py, generator_adapters.py, intake_adapters.py, test_adapters.py, capability-packs.json, agent-capability-vector.json
BI-0209 sibling pack provides established pattern.
